setup:
falcon-axi setup

Print offline guidance without writing files.

Examples:
  falcon-axi setup
  falcon-axi setup hooks
setup hooks:
falcon-axi setup hooks

Install or repair Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode session integrations.
Requires a durable installation. No network calls or skill installation.

Examples:
  falcon-axi setup hooks
  falcon-axi setup hooks --help
auth status:
falcon-axi auth status

Reports whether a credential resolved, from which channel, and which region it resolved to.
No credential value, bearer token, or tenant CID is ever printed.
config path:
falcon-axi config path [--config <path>]
Reports config and write-journal paths.
Example: falcon-axi config path
profile list:
falcon-axi profile list [--config <path>]
Lists profile names without resolving secrets.
Example: falcon-axi profile list
scopes:
falcon-axi scopes

Prints the command-to-scope matrix for provisioning the API client.
It is local only: it makes no request and needs no credential.
detection list:
falcon-axi detection list [--severity <name>] [--status <name>] [--product <name>] [--since <window>] [--filter <FQL>] [--limit N] [--cursor <token>] [--all] [--max-rows N] [--fields <names>]

--severity   one of informational, low, medium, high, critical
--status     one of new, in_progress, closed, reopened
--product    one of epp, idp, mobile, xdr, overwatch, cwpp, ngsiem, thirdparty, data-protection; epp is endpoint alerts, idp is Identity Protection
--since      relative window such as 24h or 7d
--filter     raw FQL; + is AND, `,` is OR, values are single-quoted, relative dates are lowercase
--limit      rows in this call (default 20, ceiling 10000)
--cursor     opaque continuation token from a previous call
--all        walk pages; page size is independent of --limit
--max-rows   row budget (default 1000; requires --all)
--fields     extra columns, comma-separated: status, technique, created_timestamp

Filterable fields include severity_name, status, product, tactic, technique, created_timestamp,
and device.hostname.
Identity Protection alerts have no device: their rows show the endpoint they came from as hostname
(or `n/a`) and add account, account_id, device_id, and product columns when the page holds any.
Examples:
  falcon-axi detection list --severity high --since 24h
  falcon-axi detection list --product idp --since 7d
  falcon-axi detection list --filter "severity_name:'Critical'+status:'new'"

This command is read-only and requires only Alerts:read.
detection summary:
falcon-axi detection summary [--severity <name>] [--status <name>] [--product <name>] [--since <window>] [--filter <FQL>]

--severity   one of informational, low, medium, high, critical
--status     one of new, in_progress, closed, reopened
--product    one of epp, idp, mobile, xdr, overwatch, cwpp, ngsiem, thirdparty, data-protection
--since      relative window such as 24h or 7d
--filter     raw FQL, combined with the shorthand filters as in detection list

Counts by severity across matching alerts, including hidden alerts, without listing them.
other_count, when present, counts alerts in buckets omitted by Falcon.
Examples:
  falcon-axi detection summary --since 24h
  falcon-axi detection summary --product idp --status new

This command is read-only and requires only Alerts:read.
detection show:
falcon-axi detection show <composite id> [--full]

--full       print long fields such as the command line without truncation

Example: falcon-axi detection show "ldt:aid:1234"

This command is read-only and requires only Alerts:read.
detection process:
falcon-axi detection process <composite id> [--full]

--full       print command lines without the default 800-character truncation

Show the triggering process, parent, and grandparent recorded on the alert.
Rows contain relation, filename, filepath, cmdline, sha256, and process_id.
triggering_process_graph_id is the alert's graph pivot; this view does not fetch a graph.
Absent ancestors and alerts without a process are stated explicitly.
Examples:
  falcon-axi detection process 'ldt:synthetic-agent:1001'
  falcon-axi detection process 'ldt:synthetic-agent:1001' --full

This command is read-only and requires only Alerts:read.
host list:
falcon-axi host list [--hostname <name>] [--platform <name>] [--status <name>] [--since <window>] [--filter <FQL>] [--limit N] [--cursor <token>] [--all] [--max-rows N] [--fields <names>]

--hostname   hostname to match; Hosts filters accept wildcards, so WIN-* works
--platform   one of windows, mac, linux
--status     one of normal, containment_pending, contained, lift_containment_pending
--since      last_seen within a relative window such as 24h or 7d
--filter     raw FQL; + is AND, `,` is OR, values are single-quoted, relative dates are lowercase
--limit      rows in this call (default 20, ceiling 5000)
--cursor     opaque continuation token from a previous call
--all        walk pages; page size is independent of --limit
--max-rows   row budget (default 1000; requires --all)
--fields     extra columns, comma-separated: os_version, agent_version, status, first_seen, machine_domain

Filterable fields include hostname, platform_name, os_version, agent_version, status,
last_seen, first_seen, machine_domain, and local_ip.
Examples:
  falcon-axi host list --platform windows --since 24h
  falcon-axi host list --filter "hostname:'WIN-*'+platform_name:'Windows'"

This command is read-only and requires only Hosts:read. It reports containment status as
data and cannot change it.
host show:
falcon-axi host show <device id>

The device id is the agent id Falcon calls the AID, as printed by `falcon-axi host list`.

Example: falcon-axi host show 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

This command is read-only and requires only Hosts:read.
host logins:
falcon-axi host logins <device id> [--since <window>] [--limit N]
falcon-axi host logins --hostname <pattern> [--since <window>] [--limit N]

The device id is the agent id Falcon calls the AID, as printed by `falcon-axi host list`.
--hostname   match a hostname (wildcards allowed), instead of a device id; requires exactly one match
--since      window to read, such as 24h or 7d (default 7d, Falcon's own default)
--limit      logins per host in this call (default 20, ceiling 100)

Reports recent interactive logins from the Host Timeline as device_id, user_name, and
login_time. It is a window, not a full audit trail: a host that returns its limit may have more.
Example: falcon-axi host logins abc123 --since 24h
Example: falcon-axi host logins --hostname 'synthetic-host-*' --since 24h --limit 2
Hostname form: one lookup capped at 2 IDs, then one history read; 60s total deadline.
Ambiguous or incomplete lookups fail without reading history; upstream partial errors are disclosed.

This command is read-only and requires only Hosts:read.
host network:
falcon-axi host network <device id>
falcon-axi host network --hostname <pattern>

Retrieves the IP and MAC address history Falcon retains for one sensor host.
The device id is the AID printed by `falcon-axi host list`.
--hostname   match a hostname (wildcards allowed), instead of a device id; requires exactly one match
Example: falcon-axi host network abc123
Example: falcon-axi host network --hostname 'synthetic-host-*'
Hostname form: one lookup capped at 2 IDs, then one history read; 60s total deadline.
Ambiguous or incomplete lookups fail without reading history; upstream partial errors are disclosed.
Read-only; requires Hosts:read. This endpoint has no pagination parameters.
ioc list:
falcon-axi ioc list [--filter <FQL>] [--limit N] [--cursor <token>]

--filter  FQL on type, value, action, source, severity_number, expired, created_on, modified_on
--limit   rows per call (default 20, ceiling 500)
--cursor  opaque continuation token

Examples:
  falcon-axi ioc list --filter "type:'domain'+expired:false"
  falcon-axi ioc list --limit 100

Read-only; requires IOC Management:read.
ioc show:
falcon-axi ioc show <id>

Example: falcon-axi ioc show <id>

Read-only; requires IOC Management:read.
ioc hosts:
falcon-axi ioc hosts <type:value> [--limit N] [--cursor <token>]

Types: domain, ipv4, ipv6, md5, sha256. IPv6 values retain their colons.
--limit   identifiers per call (default 20, ceiling 100)
--cursor  opaque continuation token

Returns observed identifiers; no process details or actions are requested.
Example: falcon-axi ioc hosts domain:example.invalid
Read-only; requires IOCs (Indicators of Compromise):read.
ioc processes:
falcon-axi ioc processes <type:value> --host <device_id> [--limit N] [--cursor <token>]

Types: domain, ipv4, ipv6, md5, sha256. IPv6 values retain their colons.
--limit   identifiers per call (default 20, ceiling 100)
--cursor  opaque continuation token
--host    required device ID; use ioc hosts to find it

Returns observed identifiers; no process details or actions are requested.
Example: falcon-axi ioc processes domain:example.invalid --host <device_id>
Read-only; requires IOCs (Indicators of Compromise):read.
file-change list:
falcon-axi file-change list [--filter <FQL>] [--limit N] [--cursor <token>]

Read FileVantage change history, newest action_timestamp first.
--filter   raw FQL; for example host.name:'SYNTHETIC-HOST' or action_timestamp:>'now-7d'
--limit    rows per call (default 20, ceiling 5000); hydration uses batches of 500 ids
--cursor   opaque after token bound to the query, sort, region, tenant and credential
change_ids lists identifiers in the same order as the compact rows.
Read-only; requires Falcon FileVantage:read and Falcon FileVantage licensing.
Empty results can mean no matching changes or no FileVantage license.
Captured file contents are excluded.

Example: falcon-axi file-change list --filter "host.name:'SYNTHETIC-HOST'"
file-change show:
falcon-axi file-change show <id>

Show change metadata, process fields and the documented diff object.
The id comes from change_ids in `falcon-axi file-change list`.
Read-only; requires Falcon FileVantage:read and Falcon FileVantage licensing.
Captured file contents are excluded; no content download is performed.

Example: falcon-axi file-change show 00000000000000000000000000000001
process show:
falcon-axi process show <pid-id> [--full]

ID shape: pid:<32 hex device ID>:<decimal ID>; use ioc processes to find it.
Returns command_line, device_id, file_name, process_id, process_id_local,
start_timestamp, start_timestamp_raw, stop_timestamp, and stop_timestamp_raw.
--full  expand the command line beyond its 800-character preview

Examples:
  falcon-axi process show pid:00000000000000000000000000000001:1234
  falcon-axi process show pid:00000000000000000000000000000001:1234 --full

Read-only; requires IOCs (Indicators of Compromise):read.
Availability depends on the tenant's subscription and API client permissions.
process tree:
falcon-axi process tree <pid-id> [--cursor <token>] [--full]

Shows the process first, then up to 5 ancestors in parent order, then one child level.
Children use a fixed 100-edge page; --cursor continues children for the same process.
--full    complete command lines (default preview 800 characters)
--cursor  opaque child continuation token; lineage is read again on each page

Examples:
  falcon-axi process tree pid:synthetic-device:1234
  falcon-axi process tree pid:synthetic-device:1234 --full

Read-only; requires Threatgraph:read and a subscription with ThreatGraph API access.
Response shape source: CrowdStrike SDK sample falconpy samples/threat_graph/threat_finder.py,
not a resource schema in the API spec; source-matched and tested offline, not tenant-validated.

account list:
falcon-axi account list [--filter <FQL>] [--limit N] [--cursor <token>] [--all] [--max-rows N]

--filter     raw FQL; + is AND, `,` is OR, values are single-quoted
--limit      rows in this call (default 20, ceiling 100)
--cursor     opaque continuation token from a previous call
--all        walk pages; page size is independent of --limit
--max-rows   row budget (default 1000; requires --all)

Lists the accounts Falcon Discover has observed logging in on endpoints, which is an
endpoint-observed inventory and not an identity directory.
Filterable fields include username, account_name, account_type, login_domain, user_sid,
admin_privileges, local_admin_privileges, first_seen_timestamp, password_last_set_timestamp,
last_successful_login_timestamp, and last_failed_login_timestamp.
Examples:

  falcon-axi account list --filter "username:'svc-*'"

This command is read-only and requires only Assets:read, which is license-gated to Falcon
Discover or Exposure Management.
account show:
falcon-axi account show <account id>

The account id is the identifier printed by `falcon-axi account list`.

Example: falcon-axi account show abc123

This command is read-only and requires only Assets:read, which is license-gated to Falcon
Discover or Exposure Management.
application list:
falcon-axi application list [--filter <FQL>] [--limit N] [--cursor <token>] [--fields <names>] [--full]

Returns every available application field, including nested host and usage details.
--filter     raw FQL on name, vendor, version, and host.hostname
             default name:'*' (all named applications)
--limit      rows in this call (default 20, ceiling 1000)
--cursor     opaque continuation token from a previous call
--fields     select comma-separated top-level response fields, e.g. id,name,version,host
             replaces the full row; missing selected fields are null
--full       print strings beyond the default 500-character preview

Name/vendor/version matching is exact on the whole value and case-insensitive.
Wildcards and partial names are not supported for searches; 0 rows does not prove absence.
The default name:'*' is the broad inventory query, not a partial-name search.
Use + for AND and lists for alternatives: name:['Node.js','Python'].
Spotlight does not accept apps.* filters. For hosts affected by known CVEs, use:
  falcon-axi vuln list --filter "cve.id:['CVE-2026-0001']" --fields product --all

Examples:
  falcon-axi application list --filter "name:'Node.js'+version:'24.18.0'" --fields name,version,host
  falcon-axi application list --filter "name:['Node.js','Python']"
  falcon-axi application list --filter "host.hostname:'<hostname>'"

Read-only; requires Assets:read (Falcon Discover or Exposure Management).
asset list:
falcon-axi asset list [--filter <FQL>] [--limit N] [--cursor <token>]

Lists Discover managed and unmanaged assets, distinct from Falcon sensor hosts.
--filter     raw FQL, including entity_type, hostname, platform_name, and criticality
             default id:'*' (all Discover assets)
--limit      rows in this call (default 20, ceiling 1000)
--cursor     opaque continuation token from a previous call

Examples:
  falcon-axi asset list --filter "entity_type:'managed'"
  falcon-axi asset list --filter "entity_type:'unmanaged'"

Read-only; requires Assets:read (Falcon Discover or Exposure Management).
asset show:
falcon-axi asset show <id>

Shows one Discover asset's platform, sensor association, network addresses, and observation times.
Use the Discover id from asset list, which is distinct from a Falcon device id.
Example: falcon-axi asset show synthetic-asset-01
Read-only; requires Assets:read (Falcon Discover or Exposure Management).

Read weekly sensor usage reports. Requires Sensor Usage:read.
--filter     raw FQL; supported fields include event_date and period
Returns all weekly reports supplied by Falcon; no limit, cursor or entity detail endpoint.
Reports retain all metric categories so numeric zero values remain visible.
Examples:

  falcon-axi sensor-usage list --filter "event_date:'2026-10-11'"

falcon-axi cloud-asset show <id>

cloud-risk list:

--sort     upstream sort expression, for example cloud_provider.asc

container list:
falcon-axi container list [--filter <FQL>] [--limit N] [--cursor <token>]

Lists Kubernetes containers in fixed container_name.asc order.
--filter     FQL fields include container_id, cluster_name, namespace, running_status
--limit      rows per call (default 20, ceiling 200)
--cursor     opaque continuation token; keep the same filter and credential
Falcon exposes at most 10000 records per query; narrow --filter at that boundary.
Examples:
  falcon-axi container list --filter "namespace:'production'"
  falcon-axi container list --limit 100

Read-only; requires Falcon Container Image:read and the corresponding license.
cve list:
falcon-axi cve list [--filter <FQL>] [--severity <name>] [--since <window>] [--limit N] [--cursor <token>]

Lists Falcon Intelligence CVEs, not tenant host exposure.
--filter     raw FQL, combined with shorthand filters using AND
--severity   one of low, medium, high, critical
--since      publish_date within a relative window such as 24h or 7d
--limit      rows in this call (default 20, CLI cap 100; API maximum is undocumented)
--cursor     opaque continuation token from a previous call

Default columns are cve, severity, cvss_v3_score, and exploit_status.
Filterable fields include cve, severity, publish_date, updated_timestamp, and exploit_status.
Examples:
  falcon-axi cve list --severity critical --since 7d
  falcon-axi cve list --filter "exploit_status:'unproven'"

This command is read-only and requires Vulnerabilities (Falcon Intelligence):read.
That scope requires a Falcon Intelligence subscription; Spotlight's Vulnerabilities:read does not satisfy it.
cve show:
falcon-axi cve show <CVE-ID>

Reads one CVE from Falcon Intelligence. It is not Spotlight host exposure:
an empty result means CrowdStrike Intelligence has no entry, not that no host is affected.
A CVE identifier matches CVE-<year>-<number>, for example CVE-2021-44228.

Default fields are cve, severity, cvss_v3_score, exploit_status, publish_date, updated,
and description. Related actor, report, threat, and affected-product lists are counts.
This command does not expand those lists. Run `falcon-axi cve list` to find CVEs.

Example: falcon-axi cve show CVE-2021-44228

This command is read-only and requires Vulnerabilities (Falcon Intelligence):read.
That scope is license-gated. Spotlight's Vulnerabilities:read does not satisfy it, and a
scope missing from the API client picker means the tenant has no Falcon Intelligence subscription.
Whether --member-cid carries this scope is unverified.

serverless list:
falcon-axi serverless list --filter <FQL> [--limit N] [--cursor <token>]

Reads serverless function vulnerabilities as SARIF runs in fixed cve_id order.
--filter     required FQL; fields include cloud_provider, cve_id, runtime, severity
--limit      source records per call (default 20, CLI cap 100)
--cursor     opaque continuation token; keep the same filter and credential

vuln list:
falcon-axi vuln list [--host <device id>] [--severity <name>] [--status <name>] [--since <window>] [--filter <FQL>] [--limit N] [--cursor <token>] [--fields <names>] [--all] [--max-rows N]

--host       device id (AID) whose vulnerabilities to read
--severity   one of low, medium, high, critical
--status     one of open, closed, reopen, expired
--since      created_timestamp within a relative window such as 24h or 7d
--filter     raw FQL; + is AND, `,` is OR, values are single-quoted
--limit      rows in this call (default 20, ceiling 5000)
--cursor     opaque continuation token from a previous call
--all        walk pages; page size is independent of --limit
--max-rows   row budget (default 1000; requires --all)
--fields     extra columns, comma-separated: description, base_score, exprt_rating, status, created, updated, product, remediation, platform, os, local_ip

Default columns are id, cve, severity, and hostname. --fields adds columns from that
allowlist; an unknown name is refused and the valid names are listed.
A filter is required, from a shorthand flag or --filter, because Spotlight requires one.
Wildcards are unsupported and a `*` is refused before the request is made.
Filterable fields include aid, cve.id, cve.severity, cve.exprt_rating, cve.exploit_status,
status, and created_timestamp.
Examples:
  falcon-axi vuln list --severity critical --status open
  falcon-axi vuln list --filter "status:'open'+cve.exploit_status:'90'"

This command is read-only and requires only Vulnerabilities:read.

raw get:
falcon-axi raw get --path <api-path> [--query <key=value&...>] [--query-file <file|->]

Sends one GET to the selected profile's Falcon cloud and prints the status, content type and body as TOON.
The path must be an absolute RFC 3986 path without dot segments, repeated slashes, query or fragment.
Use --query-file for secret query values; --query rejects secret-named keys. The file or stdin (-) must contain a JSON object of strings or string arrays.
One request per invocation, never replayed: no pagination, no continuation cursor, no field selection. Responses are capped at 4 MiB and binary bodies are refused.
Secret values are redacted and every field is kept, including the value beside a key that names a secret.
Examples:
  falcon-axi raw get --path /devices/queries/devices/v1 --query 'limit=5'
  falcon-axi raw get --path /detects/queries/detects/v1 --query 'filter=severity:>50&limit=2'
raw write:
falcon-axi raw write --method POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE --path <api-path> [--query <key=value&...>] [--query-file <file|->] [--body-file <file|->] [--execute --confirm '<confirm>']

Default: local preview, no network request. The preview prints the exact confirm value.
Requires a file profile with writes.allowWrites=true and "raw-write" in writes.operations, even to preview.
Execution also needs --execute and the exact --confirm value; FALCON_AXI_READ_ONLY always forbids execution.
One request, never replayed. A private redacted journal records the intent before sending and the outcome after; it is mandatory.
Use --query-file for secret query values; --query rejects secret-named keys. The file or stdin (-) must contain a JSON object of strings or string arrays.
The body is one JSON object or array of at most 1 MiB, from a file or stdin (-), without duplicate members at any depth. Query and body cannot both read stdin.
The same path syntax rules as raw get apply. Falcon authorizes the selected route.
Raw writes read no target state and detect no no-ops; reconcile an unknown outcome in the Falcon console before retrying.
Examples:
  falcon-axi raw write --method PATCH --path /example/entities/thing/v1 --body-file body.json --profile ops
  falcon-axi raw write --method PATCH --path /example/entities/thing/v1 --body-file body.json --profile ops --execute --confirm '<confirm>'
rtr run:
falcon-axi rtr run <device_id> --command '<complete command>' [--execute --confirm '<device_id>:<complete command>']

Default: local preview, no network request. Requires one 32-hex device id.
Execution requires profile rtr.enabled=true and exact host:command confirmation.
FALCON_AXI_READ_ONLY always forbids execution; previews remain available.
50-second execution budget; separate 10-second mandatory session deletion budget.
Output caps: 64 KiB and 64 status requests; incomplete/truncated output is explicit.
A durable private redacted journal is mandatory; no offline queue, pulse, or replay.
Falcon rejects a command that the host's platform lacks as Command not found.
Verified on both Windows and Linux: cat, cd, env, filehash, ls, mount, netstat, ps.
Verified on Windows only: eventlog, getsid, ipconfig, reg query.
Verified on Linux only: ifconfig, users.
Accepted on neither Windows nor Linux, because it is a macOS command and macOS was not tested: csrutil.
eventlog permits only view and list; help, clear and history exist only in the interactive console.
No shell syntax; eventlog backup/export, scripts, and file transfers are excluded.
Examples:
  falcon-axi rtr run aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa --command ps --profile triage
  falcon-axi rtr run aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa --command ps --profile triage --execute --confirm 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa:ps'
